items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Well I’m a fan of Lester Young and his lingo, and Lenny Bruce, and Lord Buckley, and all those hipsters.

ctx.x: But I wonder if your attitude about the music would have been different. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

I wouldn’t have known half of the stuff that I found out the best way, from experience. The experience is the best teacher. The tuition is very high. Yeah. But it’s worth it ‘cause if they pluck you out of a music school, you might know how to play or execute, and then they make you leader. Well you don’t even know how to be a sideman. How can you be a leader if you’ve never been a sideman? And if you’ve never worked for a good leader and a bad leader, how do you know what it is to be a good leader? If you’ve…

Well how the heck does a student these days learn that protocol? You had sort of mentioned that in today’s jazz education it seems that there are some people are now teaching who weren’t able to participate in that learning process. So you have mostly book-schooled professors now teaching another generation.

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: But I do a bit by Lenny Bruce that Lenny did with Steve Allen.

ctx.x: That’s just what I was thinking about. Like that song, “I Can’t Get Started,” he’s talking about the Prince of Wales and starting a revolution in Spain.

Right. I mean I think those are great lyrics. I don’t know if everybody will get it or if they will go oh this is dated. I mean I don’t mind dated. I don’t mind the reference to something that happened in a different time. Lenny Bruce did a thing one time where he said, “I feel just like Walli Simpson.” And I’m like, Walli Simpson? Who’s Walli Simpson? Wallis Simpson was the woman who the Prince of England fell in love with and gave up his throne for. Well I didn’t get it until I started to figure it — I…

question, —when cabs don’t drive around the park — there’s a song — when cabs don’t drive around the park, “Will You Still be Mine.” There’s some great references to, I mean when you hear the lyric you feel 1945 New York City. To me that’s nice. But if it excludes everybody —
